newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian held for US boy murder under house arrest.
newsitem.headline: Italian held for US boy murder under house arrest.

text.p: An Italian man on trial for the killing of a seven-year-old boy in a motorway hold-up, was allowed to leave jail on Tuesday on health grounds, court sources said.

A tribunal in the southern town of Catanzaro ruled that Francesco Mesiano, 23, could leave prison. Mesiano, who has been suffering violent headaches, back problems and anxiety attacks, was placed under strict house arrest.
The decision followed the release last month of co-defendant Michele Iannello, 28, by a review tribunal pending a verdict on the killing of Nicholas Green, who was shot in September 1994.

Iannello and Mesiano both deny involvement in the killing. Iannello has, however, supplied evidence for the state in other murder cases and was taken by police to an undisclosed safe house where he will live under a witness protection scheme.
Nicholas was on holiday in southern Italy with his family, from Bodega Bay, California, when their hired car was chased and shot at on a motorway in an attempted hold-up.
He was hit in the head as he slept on the back seat next to his sister.
The family's apparent lack of rancour and their decision to donate the boy's organs, which saved the lives of six young Italians, stunned Italy and earned the Greens deep respect.
The trial resumes on January 13 and the court is expected to reach a verdict by the end of January.
